findings.claim: TidyFindings reads every removed `<path> <version>` line of the go.mod diff as a removed requirement. A version bump that tidy makes (`-require x v1.0.0` / `+require x v1.1.0`) or an `// indirect` entry that moves between blocks is reported as a requirement the head no longer needs. These are false positives that the sweeper must answer `live`. The comment documents only the exclude/retract case, not the bump or move cases. No data is lost and the delivery is not blocked.
proof_refs: engine/review/sweep_test.go:561-585 (the test only covers a removal paired with an unrelated added line)

evidence: Read engine/cmd/review_sweep.go:40 via grep. The analyzers' Environ is d.environment(), the process environment, so go gets its caches and HOME as deadcode and staticcheck already do.

Tidy returns nil and nil when the copy has no go.mod, and ErrToolDidNotRun when go is missing, exits non-zero without a diff, or hits the deadline. This is covered by tests in analyzers_test.go and sweep_test.go.
Module selection (go.mod or go.sum changed, or a non-stdlib import spec removed from a .go file) reuses innermostModule and the existing ChangedLines call.
Only lines that occur more times at the head than at the base count as findings, so tidy drift that already existed at the base is filtered out.

Risk item 5 (delivery or environment): `go mod tidy -diff` needs Go 1.23 or newer and the module cache, otherwise the sweep exits 2 and the delivery stops. This is documented in the usage text, README and CHANGELOG and tested. It is not a defect.
